words.definition: to read your writing carefully to find and correct small mistakes
words.example: Always {proofread} your essay for spelling mistakes before you hand it in.

words.definition: a short text that gives only the main points
words.example: Write a short {summary} of the chapter, giving only its main points.

words.definition: extra time that you are allowed to finish a piece of work
words.example: I was ill, so my teacher gave me a three-day {extension} to finish my essay.

words.definition: to read something quickly to get the main ideas, not every detail
words.example: There's no time to read it all, so just {skim} the text for the main points.

words.definition: a drawing of ideas joined by lines to one main idea in the middle
words.example: My {mind map} had the topic in the middle, with lines joining it to all my ideas.

words.definition: to study a lot in a very short time just before an exam
words.example: He did no work all year, so now he has to {cram} the night before the exam.

words.definition: a short note at the bottom of a page that explains something in the text
words.example: The {footnote} at the bottom of the page explains where the quotation comes from.

words.definition: an early version of a piece of writing, not yet finished
words.example: This is only a first {draft}; I will check and improve it before I hand it in.

words.definition: a list at the back of a book that shows on which pages each topic appears
words.example: Look up volcanoes in the {index} at the back to find which pages mention them.

words.definition: a way of thinking about something
words.example: From my {point of view}, school should start an hour later.

words.definition: to say firmly that something must happen or is true, even when others disagree
words.example: My parents {insist} on meeting my friends before I go to their houses.

words.definition: supporting an idea or a plan
words.example: Most students voted {in favour of} a longer lunch break.

words.definition: to think that something is probably not true or will probably not happen
words.example: I {doubt} that he really met a famous footballer; he tells a lot of stories.

words.definition: to disagree with a plan and try to stop it
words.example: Many parents {oppose} the plan to close the village school and have signed a petition against it.

words.definition: more than half of the people or things in a group
words.example: Twenty of the thirty students voted yes, so the {majority} wanted the trip.

words.definition: something that you feel sure is true
words.example: Grandma has a strong {belief} that walking under a ladder brings bad luck, but there's no proof.

words.definition: easy to see or understand
words.example: The answer was so {obvious} that everyone laughed at the question.

words.definition: to say that something is not true, especially when someone says you did something wrong
words.example: My brother tried to {deny} breaking the vase, but he was still holding the pieces.

words.definition: used to introduce the first point in a list
words.example: I have two reasons: {firstly}, it's cheaper, and secondly, it's much quicker.

words.definition: every time that
words.example: My friend is late {whenever} we arrange to meet, so I always bring a book.

words.definition: used to suggest another possibility
words.example: You can take the bus; {alternatively}, you could walk, which only takes twenty minutes.

words.definition: also, and this adds to what was just said
words.example: The hotel was cheap; {moreover}, it was close to the beach.

words.definition: earlier than a particular event or time
words.example: The film starts at eight, so let's have dinner {beforehand}.

words.definition: as soon as; after
words.example: Yesterday, Sam went outside to play {once} he had finished his homework.

words.definition: but; used to compare two different facts
words.example: Cats sleep most of the day, {whereas} dogs need lots of exercise.

words.definition: in order to make something possible
words.example: Speak slowly {so that} everyone in the room can understand you.

words.definition: considering everything; in general
words.example: There were a few problems, but {overall} the school trip was a great success.

words.definition: the food that you usually eat
words.example: A healthy {diet} includes plenty of fruit and vegetables.

words.definition: harm done to the body, for example in an accident
words.example: He hurt his knee in a fall, and the {injury} kept him out for six matches.

words.definition: a visit to a doctor or dentist to make sure you are healthy
words.example: I'm not ill; it's just my yearly {check-up} at the dentist.

words.definition: (of a cut or a broken bone) to become healthy again
words.example: Keep the cut clean and it should {heal} in about a week.

words.definition: a doctor's note saying which medicine you need
words.example: The doctor gave me a {prescription} to take to the chemist.

words.definition: an area of small red spots on the skin
words.example: After eating strawberries, she got an itchy red {rash} all over her arms.

words.definition: an illness that sometimes makes it hard to breathe
words.example: My brother has {asthma}, so he always carries an inhaler when he goes running.

words.definition: extremely tired
words.example: After running the marathon, she was completely {exhausted}.

words.definition: a session of physical exercise
words.example: I do a twenty-minute {workout} every morning: press-ups, sit-ups and skipping.

words.definition: the way the Earth's weather is changing because of what people do
words.example: Hotter summers and rising sea levels are signs of {climate change}.

words.definition: not harmful to the environment
words.example: These {eco-friendly} bags are made from old bottles and can be used again and again.

words.definition: coal, oil and gas, formed from plants and animals long ago
words.example: Coal and oil are {fossil fuels} formed millions of years ago.

words.definition: made dirty and harmful by chemicals, rubbish or smoke
words.example: Nobody swims in the river now; it is too {polluted} after the factory spilled oil.

words.definition: a period of unusually hot weather
words.example: During the {heatwave}, it was over thirty-five degrees for ten days in a row.

words.definition: to change from solid to liquid because of heat
words.example: Ice cream starts to {melt} quickly when you leave it in the sun.

words.definition: a large fire that spreads quickly through forests or countryside
words.example: The dry wind spread the {wildfire} across the hills, and hundreds of families left their homes.

words.definition: a very large mass of ice that moves slowly down a mountain
words.example: The {glacier} has shrunk so much that the ice no longer reaches the valley.

words.definition: no longer existing anywhere
words.example: Dinosaurs became {extinct} millions of years ago.

words.definition: to watch or listen to something on the internet without saving it first
words.example: We {stream} films on the TV instead of buying DVDs.

words.definition: what you type, with a password, to show an app or website who you are
words.example: Enter your {username} and password to log in to the school website.

words.definition: a short message from an app that tells you something new has happened
words.example: My phone shows a {notification} every time someone likes my photo.

words.definition: the part of an app or device where you choose how it works
words.example: Go to {settings} and turn the volume down if the app is too loud.

words.definition: a cable or plug used to put power into a phone's battery
words.example: My phone is nearly dead; can I borrow your {charger}?

words.definition: being unkind to someone again and again by phone or online
words.example: Sending someone nasty messages online again and again is {cyberbullying}.

words.definition: the time you spend looking at a phone, computer or TV
words.example: My parents limit my {screen time} to two hours a day.

words.definition: emails you did not ask for, sent to lots of people, usually adverts
words.example: I delete all the {spam} in my inbox without opening it, as it might be dangerous.

words.definition: to type your name and password to start using a website
words.example: You need a password to {log in} to the school website.

words.definition: the first page of a newspaper, with the most important stories
words.example: The story was so important that it was on the {front page} of every newspaper.

words.definition: a person whose job is to find and write the news
words.example: A {journalist} interviewed the mayor about the new park.

words.definition: a series of audio shows that you can download and listen to
words.example: I listen to a science {podcast} on the bus every morning.

words.definition: a story that people pass on but that may not be true
words.example: I heard a {rumour} that our school is closing, but I have no idea whether it is true.

words.definition: to make sure that what a story says is true before you believe or share it
words.example: Before you share a shocking post, {fact-check} it on a trusted news website.

words.definition: a person who watches television or videos
words.example: As a regular {viewer} of the show, I've watched every episode since it started.

words.definition: spread very quickly from person to person online
words.example: The video of the dancing cat went {viral} overnight.

words.definition: not real, but made to look real
words.example: That photo is {fake}: someone changed it on a computer to make it look real.

words.definition: unfairly supporting one side more than the other
words.example: The report was {biased} because it only gave one side of the story.

words.definition: money you are paid for each hour, day or week that you work
words.example: The café pays its staff a weekly {wage} based on how many hours they work.

words.definition: a period of work, for example during the day or the night
words.example: Nurses often work a night {shift} from eight in the evening until eight in the morning.

words.definition: a written legal agreement, for example between a worker and a company
words.example: Read your {contract} carefully before you sign it; it says how many hours you will work.

words.definition: to ask formally, usually in writing, for a job or a place
words.example: She wants to {apply} for a summer job at the café.

words.definition: working only some of the day or week
words.example: My sister has a {part-time} job at weekends.

words.definition: a person you work with
words.example: She went for lunch with a {colleague}, one of the people she works with every day.

words.definition: extra hours that you work after your normal working day
words.example: He worked three hours of {overtime} on Friday to finish the project.

words.definition: the time when you stop working, usually because you are old
words.example: After forty years as a teacher, she is looking forward to her {retirement}.

words.definition: without a paid job
words.example: After the factory closed, many people were {unemployed}.

words.definition: a small sum that parents give their child, often every week, to spend
words.example: My parents give me five pounds of {pocket money} every Saturday, and I save it for games.

words.definition: money that you pay to join something or to use a service
words.example: The {fee} to join the football club is thirty pounds a year.

words.definition: to have enough money to buy something
words.example: We can't {afford} a holiday abroad this year.

words.definition: a small label on a product that shows how much it costs
words.example: Check the {price tag} on that jacket before you try it on.

words.definition: a bank account for money you want to keep, which slowly earns extra money
words.example: I put my birthday money into a {savings account} so that it would grow.

words.definition: a piece of paper or a code that you can use instead of money in a particular shop
words.example: For my birthday, Gran gave me a book {voucher} worth twenty pounds.

words.definition: money that you borrow and must pay back
words.example: They took out a bank {loan} to buy the house.

words.definition: a machine in a wall that gives you money from your bank account
words.example: Put your card in the {cash machine} outside the bank and type your PIN.

words.definition: something bought for much less than its usual price
words.example: These boots were a {bargain}: I paid only five pounds for something worth fifty.

words.definition: how much of one country's money you get for another country's money
words.example: With today's {exchange rate}, my hundred pounds became a hundred and fifteen euros.

words.definition: special glasses that protect your eyes
words.example: Put on your safety {goggles} before heating anything over the flame.

words.definition: to find the size or amount of something
words.example: Use a ruler to {measure} the length of the leaf.

words.definition: to watch something carefully
words.example: Through the lens, we could {observe} tiny creatures moving.

words.definition: something made by putting two or more things together
words.example: Salt water is a {mixture} because it is made of two different things.

words.definition: a solid, a liquid or a gas of a particular kind
words.example: Salt is a white {substance} that dissolves in water.

words.definition: to mix into a liquid and disappear
words.example: Stir the sugar into cold water and it will slowly {dissolve} until you cannot see it.

words.definition: the gas in the air that we need to breathe
words.example: Plants give out {oxygen} during the day.

words.definition: an instrument that makes very small things look much bigger
words.example: We looked at onion cells under a {microscope}.

words.definition: a piece of metal that pulls iron towards it
words.example: The {magnet} picked up all the paper clips.

words.definition: to change from a liquid into a gas
words.example: In the sun, the puddles soon {evaporate}.

words.definition: the place at an airport where you show your ticket and leave your big bags
words.example: When you arrive at the airport, go to {check-in} first and leave your big suitcase there.

words.definition: a small place to stay, often run by a family in their own home
words.example: We stayed at a little {guesthouse} by the sea, run by a friendly couple.

words.definition: for or during the night
words.example: We travelled {overnight} on the train and woke up in Scotland.

words.definition: visiting famous places as a tourist
words.example: We spent the whole day {sightseeing} in Rome.

words.definition: a document, on paper or on your phone, that you must show to get on a plane
words.example: Show your {boarding pass} at the gate before you get on the plane.

words.definition: a short trip, often organised for a group on holiday
words.example: On the third day of our holiday we went on an {excursion} to an old castle.

words.definition: a person who travels cheaply, carrying their things in a big bag on their back
words.example: A {backpacker} carries everything in one big bag and stays in cheap hostels.

words.definition: the place at a border where officials check what you bring into a country
words.example: At {customs}, an officer opened our suitcase to check what we had brought into the country.

words.definition: a tired feeling after flying to a place where the time is different
words.example: After flying to Tokyo, my body clock was confused and I had terrible {jet lag}.

words.definition: to believe that someone is honest and will not hurt you
words.example: I {trust} my best friend with all my secrets.

words.definition: a feeling that someone is good and important
words.example: Treat older people with {respect}.

words.definition: to say sorry
words.example: You should {apologise} to her for being rude.

words.definition: always telling other people what to do
words.example: My older sister is so {bossy}; she always tells me what to wear.

words.definition: always supporting a person, team or group, even in hard times
words.example: Ben stayed {loyal} to his old club, even when a richer team offered him more money.

words.definition: to have a friendly relationship with someone
words.example: I {get on with} my cousins really well.

words.definition: the feeling that you must do what people your age do
words.example: Don't give in to {peer pressure} if something feels wrong.

words.definition: to stop being angry with someone who did something wrong
words.example: It took me a long time to {forgive} him for lying.

words.definition: helping and encouraging someone, especially when things are hard
words.example: When I was nervous about my exams, my {supportive} parents kept telling me I could do it.

words.definition: friendly and enjoying meeting new people
words.example: Tom is {outgoing}: at parties he talks to everyone, even people he has never met.

words.definition: not talking much about your own skills or successes
words.example: Even after winning the gold medal, she was {modest} and said her team deserved the praise.

words.definition: thinking only about yourself
words.example: It was {selfish} of him to eat all the biscuits.

words.definition: often changing from happy to angry or sad without warning
words.example: He's very {moody}: cheerful one minute, and grumpy the next for no reason.

words.definition: putting a lot of effort into what you do
words.example: Our {hard-working} neighbour never takes a day off, yet he always seems full of energy.

words.definition: good at thinking of new and original ideas
words.example: My {creative} cousin is always inventing new games and writing her own songs.

words.definition: showing good judgement
words.example: It's {sensible} to wear a helmet when you cycle.

words.definition: relaxed and not easily worried
words.example: My dad is {easy-going}; he doesn't mind what we have for dinner.

words.definition: too interested in other people's private business
words.example: Our {nosy} neighbour always looks out of the window to see who is visiting us.

words.definition: money you must pay for breaking a rule
words.example: He got a parking {fine} for leaving his car on the pavement.

words.definition: not allowed by the law
words.example: It is {illegal} to drive without a licence.

words.definition: a person who sees a crime or an accident happen
words.example: The police need a {witness}: someone who actually saw the crash happen.

words.definition: to take someone to a police station because they may have done a crime
words.example: The police will {arrest} anyone caught stealing.

words.definition: having done something wrong or against the law
words.example: The jury decided he was {guilty}, so he was sent to prison for theft.

words.definition: not having done anything wrong
words.example: He spent years in prison before they proved he was {innocent}.

words.definition: damaging public property on purpose
words.example: Breaking the park benches was an act of {vandalism}.

words.definition: the crime of stealing
words.example: Lock your bike: {theft} is common here, and bikes often disappear from the station.

words.definition: a group of people who decide in court if someone did a crime
words.example: In court, the {jury} listened to the witness before deciding if he was guilty.

words.definition: to stop trying or stop doing something
words.example: Don't {give up} now; you're nearly at the top!

words.definition: to discover a fact
words.example: I want to {find out} who left the gate open.

words.definition: to feel happy about something that is going to happen
words.example: I {look forward to} seeing you next week.

words.definition: to decide to do something later
words.example: I always {put off} my homework until Sunday night, and then I have to rush it.

words.definition: to say no to an offer
words.example: She was offered a job abroad but decided to {turn down} the offer.

words.definition: to start a business, club or organisation
words.example: They want to {set up} a recycling club at school.

words.definition: to use all of something so that none is left
words.example: Hurry up, or we'll {run out of} time!

words.definition: to take action to solve a problem
words.example: The head teacher will {deal with} the noisy pupils.

words.definition: to think of an idea or a plan
words.example: We need to {come up with} a name for our band.

words.definition: to feel better after something bad has happened
words.example: It took him two weeks to {get over} a bad cold.

words.definition: an opinion about what someone should do
words.example: Can I give you some {advice} about your essay?

words.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do
words.example: The guide will {advise} you on which paths are safe.

words.definition: to change or influence something
words.example: Lack of sleep can {affect} your memory.

words.definition: a change that something causes
words.example: The new law had a big {effect} on traffic.

words.definition: to say yes to something you are offered
words.example: I'm happy to {accept} your invitation to the wedding.

words.definition: but not
words.example: Everyone came to the party {except} Tom, who was ill.

words.definition: to lift or move something up
words.example: Please {raise} your hand if you know the answer.

words.definition: to go up
words.example: We watched the smoke {rise} slowly from the chimney.

words.definition: pens, paper, envelopes and other things for writing
words.example: The {stationery} cupboard is full of pens and paper.
